style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: The missionary benediction -- Aaron's blessing from Numbers 6 turned outward until it covers the planet. Israel asks for the shining face not to keep it but to broadcast it: bless us, THAT Your way may be known on earth and Your salvation among all nations. The refrain that frames the center is the church's oldest missions cry -- let the peoples praise You, O God; let ALL the peoples praise You -- and the reason given is the joy of a just Judge: the nations will be glad because He governs them with equity. The harvest at the end (the earth has yielded its increase) suggests a thanksgiving festival setting, and the logic runs both ways: a blessed people is God's advertisement, and a blessed harvest is meant to make the ends of the earth fear Him. Seven verses, and every one of them refuses to let the blessing stop at Israel's border.

1.text: For the choir director, on stringed instruments. A psalm, a song. May God show us grace and bless us; may He make His face shine on us -- Selah --
1.amp: To the chief Musician [natsach] on Neginoth [neginah -- stringed instruments], A Psalm [mizmor] or Song [shir]. God [Elohim] be merciful [chanan -- gracious] unto us, and bless [barak] us; and cause His face [panim] to shine [or] upon ['with', the KJV margin] us; Selah [selah].
1.notes: The Aaronic blessing prayed back to God in the congregation's voice (cf. Numbers 6:24-26): chanan, barak, or panim (H2603, H1288, H215) -- grace, blessing, the shining face. But note the name: Elohim, the God of all peoples, not the covenant YHWH -- the psalm is already looking past the camp.

2.text: so that Your way may be known on the earth, and Your salvation among all the nations.
2.amp: That Your way [derek] may be known [yada] upon earth [eretz], Your saving health [yeshuah -- Your salvation] among all nations [goy].
2.notes: The purpose clause that turns a benediction into a mission: bless us THAT -- la-daat, so that it be known -- Your derek on eretz and Your yeshuah (H3444) among kol goyim (H1471). Israel asked to be blessed as a display window (cf. Genesis 12:2-3; Acts 13:47).

3.text: Let the peoples give You thanks, O God; let all the peoples give You thanks!
3.amp: Let the people [am] praise [yadah] You, O God [Elohim]; let all the people [am] praise You.
3.notes: The refrain, and the widening within it: ammim, then KOL ammim -- the peoples, then all of them, no nation excused. yadah (H3034) is thanksgiving-praise: the Gentiles not merely subdued but grateful.

4.text: Let the nations be glad and sing for joy, for You judge the peoples with equity and guide the nations on the earth. Selah.
4.amp: O let the nations [leom] be glad [samach] and sing for joy [ranan]: for You shall judge [shaphat] the people [am] righteously [mishor -- with equity, on the level], and govern ['lead', nachah, the KJV margin] the nations [leom] upon earth [eretz]. Selah.
4.notes: The center of the seven, and the reason the nations should rejoice at being judged: mishor (H4334) -- level ground, straight dealing, the equity every people has begged its own rulers for. nachah (H5148) is the shepherd-verb of Psalm 23:3: the Judge of nations also their Guide.

5.text: Let the peoples give You thanks, O God; let all the peoples give You thanks!
5.amp: Let the people [am] praise [yadah] You, O God [Elohim]; let all the people [am] praise You.
5.notes: The refrain repeated to frame the center: verse 4 held inside two calls for universal thanksgiving. The structure is the theology -- God's just rule is the thing worth all the world's gratitude.

6.text: The earth has yielded its harvest; God, our own God, blesses us.
6.amp: Then shall the earth [eretz] yield [natan -- give] her increase [yebul -- produce]; and God [Elohim], even our own God, shall bless [barak] us.
6.notes: The harvest has come in -- eretz natan yebulah (H5414, H2981) -- and the blessing asked in verse 1 is now reported: Elohim Elohenu, God OUR God, the possessive finally allowed. Probably sung at the feast of ingathering, with the full barns as exhibit A.

7.text: God will bless us, and every far edge of the earth will stand in fear of Him.
7.amp: God [Elohim] shall bless [barak] us; and all the ends [ephes] of the earth [eretz] shall fear [yare] Him.
7.notes: The circle closes exactly where it opened -- barak -- but the last clause is the whole point: kol aphse eretz (H657), every far edge of the planet, brought to yare (H3372). A blessed Israel is a lit lamp; the light was always meant for the room, not the stand (cf. Matthew 5:14-16).
